method:
Two-phase probe using temporary files in src/tests/ssr-probe/ (cases.tsx, runner.tsx, server.test.tsx, hydrate.test.tsx, hydrate-reduced.test.tsx). All of them have since been deleted. Versions: React and react-dom 19.3.0, Vitest 5.0.3, react-router-dom 7.18.4, motion 14.0.0. NODE_ENV=test, so React's dev builds ran and printed full hydration diffs.

Shared cases (cases.tsx): every component case is wrapped exactly as App.tsx does it, with default props everywhere: <ColorModeProvider> (no storage/mode props, so the localStorage and matchMedia paths run) > <GlobalStyles/> > <UIProvider> > <ToastProvider> > <MemoryRouter initialEntries={['/']}>. MemoryRouter is used on both sides so the router tree is identical and cannot cause a mismatch. The ToastProvider and ColorModeProvider cases are also rendered standalone with no other providers. Extra cases: Loading inline, Sidebar permanent collapsed (tooltips), Home page (full App tree), and Modal open as the last child with only UIProvider around it.

Phase 1, server (server.test.tsx, docblock `@vitest-environment node`): the file asserts typeof window and typeof document are 'undefined' (localStorage and matchMedia were undefined too). It dynamically imports the cases, calls renderToString from react-dom/server per case inside try/catch, captures console.error/warn, and writes {name, ok, html, logs} to <scratchpad>/ssr-probe/server-html.json. The repo config could not run this file: src/tests/setup.ts:20 calls Object.defineProperty(window, ...) unconditionally and throws "ReferenceError: window is not defined" in a node environment, and Vitest 5 has no CLI override for setupFiles. So phase 1 ran with `npx vitest run --config <scratchpad>/ssr-probe/vitest.server.config.ts`. That config imports vite.config.ts and only changes root, environment='node', setupFiles=[] and include=[server.test.tsx]; plugins, aliases and css:false are unchanged, so CSS-module class names come out the same in both environments.

Phase 2, hydration (jsdom, normal repo config including setup.ts, run with `npx vitest run src/tests/ssr-probe/hydrate`): the runner sets IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT and installs its own window.matchMedia and innerWidth. For each case it clears localStorage and seeds it per variant, resets document.body and <html data-theme>, and puts the server HTML into <div id="root"> on body. It spies on console.error/warn and calls hydrateRoot(container, sameElement, {onRecoverableError, onCaughtError, onUncaughtError}) inside `await act(async () => ...)`, then flushes with a second act and a 30ms timer. It records recoverable errors with their message and component stack, console errors and warnings, how many server DOM nodes survived (to detect a client re-render), and portal output outside the container, then unmounts.

Required variant A: width 1280 (min-width:768px matches), prefers-color-scheme: dark true, localStorage['enchase-color-mode']='dark', reduced motion false. Isolation variants: B mobile 375 + light + nothing stored (control); C desktop + light + nothing stored; D mobile + dark system + nothing stored; F mobile + light system + stored 'dark'; E mobile + light + prefers-reduced-motion. E ran in its own test file because motion caches the reduced-motion preference per module graph.

Results JSON: <scratchpad>/ssr-probe/hydration-{A..F}-*.json. 'hydration' below reports variant A. Status rule: a recoverable/uncaught error or a hydration-mismatch console.error counts as 'mismatch', and 'error' was reserved for thrown or uncaught errors (none happened).

results.hydrationDetail: Clean in A, B, C, D and F (4/4 server nodes kept). Only in variant E (client prefers reduced motion), console.error reports an attribute mismatch that React does not patch: the server <button> has tabindex="0" and the client does not.
results.cause: Variant A: none. Variant E: src/hooks/useMotionRecipe.ts:11 `useReducedMotion() ?? false` is null on the server and true on a reduced-motion client. src/motion/recipes.ts:98-100 then maps 'press' to {}, so motion.button in src/components/common/Button/index.tsx:11-15 loses whileTap and stops emitting tabindex=0.

results.hydrationDetail: Clean in all variants. The useId values (_R_2q_, _R_4q_) are the same on server and client, and the password toggle hydrates.

results.cause: None observed. Latent risk: src/components/common/Tooltip/index.tsx:64-74 adds a createPortal on the client only (`typeof document !== 'undefined' &&`). It is safe only because the portal has no host children at hydration time (open is always false at first). The Modal case shows that a portal with content during hydration fails.

results.hydrationDetail: onRecoverableError: "Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client." Diff: aria-label "Mudar para tema claro" (client) vs "Mudar para tema escuro" (server); svg className "lucide lucide-sun" vs "lucide lucide-moon"; client <circle cx=12 cy=12 r=4> vs server <path d="M20.985 ...">. The whole root was client-rendered (0/8 server nodes survived). D (system dark only) and F (stored dark only) each reproduce it; B and C are clean. E produces an attribute-only mismatch: span style opacity:1 vs "opacity:1;transform:none", plus tabindex.
results.cause: ColorModeProvider resolves a different mode on the server than on the client. (1) Storage path: src/components/colorMode/defaultData.ts:13 returns null storage when window is undefined, so src/components/colorMode/index.tsx:15 starts at 'system' on the server, while the same useState initializer reads 'dark' from localStorage on the client. (2) System path: index.tsx:16 calls useMediaQuery, and src/hooks/useMediaQuery.ts:4 reads window.matchMedia(query).matches in its useState initializer (false on the server, true on the client). resolvedMode (index.tsx:18) then drives the label at src/components/common/ThemeToggle/index.tsx:15 and the keyed icon branch at :21-22 (Moon vs Sun).

results.hydrationDetail: Clean in all variants. The server outputs nothing; the client adds a portal to document.body whose AnimatePresence has no children, so hydration has nothing to match.
results.cause: None (but see Modal isOpen=true for the same code path with content).

results.hydrationDetail:
The server HTML has no dialog at all (only

Página

and the toast region). On hydration, onRecoverableError fires in every variant, including control B: "Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client...". The diff shows ModalDialog's root
being matched against the next server node, the toast region
, with an extra client child
. When the Modal is the last child (standalone case) the diff is "+
" (an extra node). The whole root was regenerated on the client (0/4 nodes kept), and the dialog then mounts into body.
results.cause: src/components/common/Modal/index.tsx:89 `if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null` renders nothing on the server, while :91-106 returns createPortal(<AnimatePresence>{isOpen && <ModalDialog/>}</AnimatePresence>, document.body) on the client. React does not support portals that have content during hydration: it tries to hydrate the portal's host nodes against the parent's server DOM, which throws. An open modal is also never part of the SSR HTML.

results.hydrationDetail: Same failure as Modal isOpen=true in every variant: the role="alertdialog" ModalDialog <div ref> is matched against the server toast-region div and the extra backdrop child throws "Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client". The root was regenerated on the client (0/4 nodes kept).
results.cause: ConfirmModal renders <Modal isOpen> (src/components/common/Modal/index.tsx:128), so it hits the same server null at :89 and client createPortal at :91.

results.hydrationDetail: Fails in every variant: "Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client". The diff shows OverlayLoading's root <div ref> compared with the server toast-region div, plus an extra client <div className="_overlay_2716ca" aria-hidden="true">. The root was regenerated on the client (0/4 nodes kept). The overlay is missing from the SSR HTML.
results.cause: src/components/common/Loading/index.tsx:42 `if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null` on the server versus :44 `createPortal(<OverlayLoading .../>, document.body)` on the client. The portal's content (OverlayLoading root div at :27-28) gets hydrated against server DOM that does not contain it.

results.hydrationDetail: "Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client". The diff is the same as ThemeToggle: aria-label "Mudar para tema claro" vs "Mudar para tema escuro" and lucide-sun <circle> vs lucide-moon <path>. The root was regenerated (0/20 nodes kept). results.cause: Navbar itself is SSR-safe. Its matchMedia use is inside useEffect at src/components/navbar/index.tsx:62-71. It embeds <ThemeToggle /> at src/components/navbar/index.tsx:91, so it inherits the ColorModeProvider divergence (src/components/colorMode/index.tsx:15-16 via src/hooks/useMediaQuery.ts:4) that feeds src/components/common/ThemeToggle/index.tsx:15,21-22.

results.cause: None observed. The year comes from new Date().getFullYear() (src/components/footer/defaultData.ts:9), which could differ between server and client only around New Year across time zones.

results.hydrationDetail: "Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client". The server rendered the mobile layout, the client the desktop one. Diff: wrapper data-sidebar="" (client) vs absent; menu button aria-label "Recolher menu lateral" vs "Abrir menu", aria-expanded true vs "false", aria-haspopup undefined vs "dialog". The structural break is in MenuToggleIcon: the client's <svg data-icon="menu-open"> with paths M3 6h13/M3 12h9/M3 18h13 plus an extra path M21 8l-4 4 4 4, against the server's lucide-menu (M4 5h16...). The ThemeToggle diff in the actions slot also applies. The root was regenerated (0/28 nodes kept). C (desktop, light, nothing stored) still fails, so the viewport alone is enough; B is clean; D and F fail through ThemeToggle; E gives attribute-only mismatches.
results.cause: Two independent causes. (1) src/components/layout/index.tsx:42 `const isDesktop = useMediaQuery('(min-width: 768px)')`: src/hooks/useMediaQuery.ts:4 initializes from window.matchMedia on the client and to false on the server. isDesktop then changes layout/index.tsx:60 (data-sidebar), :68-72 (AppBar label/expanded/haspopup/handler), :83-87 (permanent sidebar area) and :101 (modal sidebar). The first throw comes from src/components/layout/subcomponentes/MenuToggleIcon/index.tsx:23-24 (keyed open/closed icon). (2) <ThemeToggle/> in the AppBar actions (layout/index.tsx:73) carries the ColorModeProvider divergence from src/components/colorMode/index.tsx:15-16.

results.hydrationDetail: Clean in all variants, both standalone (no other providers, using the default UIContext) and inside the full App provider stack. The aria-live region with an empty AnimatePresence matches.
results.cause: None.

results.hydrationDetail: Clean in all variants. The <style> from ThemeVariables does not depend on the mode (defaultThemeCss), and data-theme and color-scheme are applied to <html> in useLayoutEffect after hydration (data-theme becomes 'dark' in A).
results.cause: No hydration error. SSR side effect: the server HTML carries no data-theme, and styles/css/declarations.ts:55 makes ":root, [data-theme='light']" the default with no prefers-color-scheme fallback. Dark-mode users therefore see the light theme until src/components/colorMode/index.tsx:34-37 runs on the client. The provider's internal state also differs (index.tsx:15-16), which breaks any consumer that renders from mode or resolvedMode (ThemeToggle, Navbar, Layout).

results.hydrationDetail: Same as Layout: data-sidebar, menu button aria attributes, and MenuToggleIcon MenuOpenIcon vs lucide-menu throw "Hydration failed...", and the whole root is regenerated (0/42 nodes kept). Clean in control B. React's hoisted <link rel="preload" as="image" href="/enchase-marca.svg"> at the top of the renderToString output was skipped correctly during hydration.
results.cause: Inherits the Layout causes: src/components/layout/index.tsx:42 with src/hooks/useMediaQuery.ts:4, plus ThemeToggle via src/components/colorMode/index.tsx:15-16.

results.hydrationDetail: In every variant: "Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client", with the diff "+ <div ref={{current:null}}>" under ModalDialog (the client inserts a node the server never sent). This shows the Modal failure does not depend on which sibling follows it.
results.cause: src/components/common/Modal/index.tsx:89 (null on the server) versus :91 (createPortal with content on the client during hydration).

notes:
All 25 cases server-rendered without throwing, and none logged a console.error or console.warn on the server. In variant A, 18 cases hydrate cleanly and 7 fail, all with a recoverable error after which the whole root is rendered again on the client. With no Suspense boundary, one failing component regenerates the entire page.

There are three root-cause families:
(a) Values read from browser storage or media queries inside useState initializers: src/hooks/useMediaQuery.ts:4 and src/components/colorMode/index.tsx:14-16 together with colorMode/defaultData.ts:13. These affect ThemeToggle, Navbar, Layout and Home.
(b) Server/client branches that return null on the server and a portal with content on the client: Modal/index.tsx:89-91 and Loading/index.tsx:42-44. These affect Modal open, ConfirmModal open and Loading overlay, and they fail even when server and client environments are identical (control variant B).
(c) Reduced motion (variant E only): hooks/useMotionRecipe.ts:11 gives attribute-only mismatches that React does not patch, in Button, ThemeToggle, Sidebar modal, Navbar and Layout.

The variant matrix shows which input triggers what. B (mobile, light, nothing stored) fails only on the portal cases. C (desktop, light, nothing stored) adds Layout and Home. D (dark system preference alone) and F (stored 'dark' alone) each add ThemeToggle, Navbar, Layout and Home.

Method caveats:
- renderToString was used instead of Next's streaming renderer.
- Hydration targets a <div id=root> container rather than hydrateRoot(document), as Next does.
- The server step needed a scratchpad config, because src/tests/setup.ts:20 throws in a node environment. That config disables setupFiles and changes nothing else.
- The zustand persist store (stores/app, key 'app-storage', which holds sidebarCollapsed) was not seeded, so its effect on hydration is untested.

Cleanup: src/tests/ssr-probe/ was deleted, and `git status --porcelain` printed nothing. Only the dist/ directory that was already there shows up as ignored. Raw data is kept in <scratchpad>/ssr-probe/ (server-html.json, hydration-A..F-*.json, vitest.server.config.ts). No commits were made and no other repository files changed.
